oil.summary: Crude markets are digesting a sharp intraday reversal after a strong weekly run. WTI settled near $79.19 (-0.23%) and Brent at $84.10 (-0.78%), both pulling back modestly despite a weekly gain of roughly 7.7% fuelled by US-Iran hostilities and Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes. The day's sharper losses were concentrated in products: RBOB gasoline cratered 5.17% and heating oil fell 4.24%, suggesting some demand-side concern is creeping in. Bearish undercurrents include China's refinery runs crashing to pandemic-era lows as crude imports collapse, and Chinese teapot refiners pivoting away from Iranian barrels toward Qatari, Iraqi, and UAE grades. On the supply side, API reported a 564,000-barrel draw in US crude inventories. The US-backed Iraq-Syria Mediterranean pipeline proposal and expanded sanctions targeting the Shamkhani network add further complexity to the supply outlook.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes and US-Iran conflict drove a ~7.7% weekly crude rally, now partially unwinding in products
China's refinery runs at pandemic lows and teapot refiners shunning Iranian crude signal weakening Asian demand and trade-flow realignment
US expands Iran sanctions (Shamkhani network) and backs Iraq-Syria pipeline bypass, reshaping medium-term supply routes

gas.summary: Natural gas headlines today are thin on sector-specific catalysts. Henry Hub slipped to $2.924/MMBtu (+0.62% on the day), but the weekly picture is sharply negative at -9.03%, consistent with a market that ran ahead of itself. The available headlines are predominantly oil-focused; no direct LNG, storage, or weather drivers were provided for US gas today. TTF, covered under Power & Carbon, tells a very different story with a 13.70% weekly surge to €52.959/MWh, likely reflecting Middle East supply anxiety feeding into European energy security concerns. Traders should note the widening US-European gas price divergence as a potential arbitrage and LNG export theme to monitor.
drivers: Henry Hub down sharply on the week (-9.03%) with no specific bullish US gas catalyst evident in today's feed
TTF surging +13.70% on the week, diverging strongly from Henry Hub amid Middle East supply disruption fears in Europe
Gas-specific news flow is limited today; oil and pipeline headlines dominate without direct Henry Hub implications

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged marginally lower to $76.70/EUA (-0.43%) on the day but remain modestly bid on the month (+1.51%) and week (+2.56%). The dominant power-sector story is TTF's sharp weekly surge of 13.70% to €52.959/MWh, driven by Middle East tension and Trump's resumption of Iran port blockades with threatened strikes on energy targets — developments that directly pressure European gas-fired generation costs. A geothermal energy piece flagged Germany's efforts to balance energy security and decarbonization amid this summer's heat wave. Bangladesh's nuclear ambitions and India's solar pivot add longer-term emerging-market power context. The bipartisan US Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026, targeting Russia's oil exports and shadow fleet, could further tighten European energy supply assumptions.
drivers: TTF +13.70% on the week as Iran conflict and port blockade threats tighten European gas supply expectations, lifting gas-fired generation costs
EU EUAs holding above €76, supported by elevated gas prices raising carbon intensity of the European power mix
New US Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 and Trump threats on Iranian energy infrastructure add upside risk to European energy supply security
